title: Ramp Resilience Harness and Customer Expectation Contract
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: build a deterministic, tenant-aware load testing harness and an accompanying benchmarking methodology that ties directly to customer-facing throughput guarantees and autoscaler policies. We will produce an operational playbook (runbook + template results) that SRE/SEPs can run during onboarding to produce a signed "throughput contract" for a customer Dedicated pool.

Scope: harness (agent + coordinator + telemetry), canonical workload library representing short-chat, long-chat, embeddings, and mixed QPS bursts, standard metrics and postprocessing, and an acceptance checklist that maps measured signals to Contract outcomes (e.g., Sustained QPS, 99th tail latency, cold-start tail). Include tenant isolation stress tests to validate QoS policies. Not in scope: new kernel-level runtime changes (those will be separate RFCs).

Deliverables: 1) ramp-resilience-harness binary + infra templates (k8s) 2) benchmark methodology doc 3) customer acceptance report template + signed contract template 4) CI smoke tests that run the harness in nightly staging and surface regressions to console-2026.03 dashboard.

Motivation: current onboarding relies on ad-hoc adoptions of various 'replay' artifacts. Customers need a reproducible, auditable artifact that demonstrates the Dedicated pool meets the throughput corridor we advertise (including burst headroom and sustained windows). This ticket unifies test artifact generation and the decision rules around pass/fail and recommended autoscaler/route configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 30m sustain scenario and produce structured outputs: per-interval QPS, p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU utilization, queue depth, error rates, and KV cache hit rate.

Methodology doc defines three canonical profiles (conversational-short, conversational-long, embeddings-heavy) with seed prompts and token distributions; profiles produce repeatable telemetry within 5% on staging hardware.
Customer acceptance report template includes a clear mapping of measured signals to the contract (Sustained QPS, Burst headroom, Tail latency SLO).
Runbook lists steps for generating the signed throughput contract and specifies mitigation actions when a pool fails (autoscaler tune, model-variant fallback, rate-limiter knobs).
Automated CI job in staging runs a smoke harness nightly; regressions create a ticket and post to #dedicated-throughput in Slack.
test_plan: 1) Provision a test Dedicated pool using the infra template. 2) Deploy coordinator + N agents across tenants to emulate tenant mixes. 3) Run baseline short-ramp (3m ramp, 27m sustain), collect telemetry. 4) Run burst profile: repeated 30s microbursts at 3x sustained QPS, validate tail behavior. 5) Run tenant-isolation stress: ramp single tenant to consume 60% of pool capacity and verify QoS for remaining tenants. 6) Verify autoscaler reactiveness: introduce steady ramp and record scale events and resulting latency curves. 7) Postprocess and populate the customer acceptance report.
